title: What do the three angles of a triangle add up to?
description: The three angles of a triangle are measured with a protractor, written near their corners and added. The same is done for the other triangles in the book, and the sums are compared.
teaching_notes: One idea: the three angles of any triangle add up to the same number. Watch for students who expect a different sum for a bigger triangle, because the arms look longer.

source: Figure it Out (after Angle Bisector), Q9
video_script.why: The child measures the three angles of triangles by the three checks of the solved example, adds them, and notices that the sum is the same each time.
video_script.substitution: The triangles of the book's question.
video_script.anchor: the triangles of the book, each with its three corners
video_script.payoff_line: The three angles of a triangle add up to one hundred and eighty degrees
maths_rules: the three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees
a measured sum may be a degree or two away from 180 because measuring is never exact
the book says it will come back to why this happens in a later year
video_script.design: The triangles stay on the board. Each is measured by the same steps, and the sum is held back until the answer line.
open_questions: The three triangles of the book are drawn figures that are not in the extracted text, so the video gives no readings for them and teaches the method and the sum only.
